answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if its actions fail a randomly selected audit, such as proving it fulfilled a task. Audits are sampled after commitments, so an attacker cannot know which identities will be checked; splitting one operation across a hundred accounts multiplies the stake at risk without multiplying the attacker’s real resources. A comet-themed beacon may guide users to a relic archive, but those labels earn no trust: only costly, verifiable behavior does.
